🇳🇵 Nepal–Tibet Border Avalanche & Flood | 26 August 2026 A major ice–rock avalanche near the Nepal–Tibet border triggered a cascading hazard: a large glacier mass collapsed from high elevation, sending ice, rock and sediment into the Lhende Khola. The debris blocked the river and formed a temporary barrier lake, which then released a powerful downstream surge of muddy water, debris and boulders. 🌡️ Possible factors: glacier instability, melting ice, steep crevassed terrain, meltwater lubrication and possible seismic triggering. ⚠️ Some claims remain unconfirmed, so the exact trigger requires scientific investigation. 🌊 Avalanche → Debris Flow → River Blockage → Dam Breach → Flood #Nepal #NepalFlood #NepalLandslide #NepalAvalanche #NepalTibetBorder Himalayas HimalayanAvalanche Landslide GlacierCollapse GlacialLake BarrierLake FlashFlood DebrisFlow LhendeKhola Bhotekoshi ClimateChange GlacierMelt NaturalDisaster DisasterScience EarthScience 26August2026

Hasta el momento se desconoce la cantidad de dinero, quién sería su verdadero propietario y qué ocurrió después de la grabación. Más que un “tesoro”, ese dinero podría representar los ahorros, el trabajo o la única esperanza de una familia que perdió su hogar durante la emergencia. Reflexión: Una tragedia no debe convertirse en una oportunidad para aprovecharse del dolor ajeno. Nuestra verdadera riqueza se encuentra en la honestidad, la empatía y la voluntad de ayudar. Lo correcto sería intentar localizar a su dueño o entregar lo encontrado a las autoridades correspondientes. 📖 “El que es fiel en lo muy poco, también en lo más es fiel.” — Lucas 16:10 🙏 Que Dios toque cada corazón y permita que las pertenencias recuperadas regresen a sus verdaderos propietarios. #rasuwa #nepal #nepalflood #rasuwaflood #flood  After the Rasuwa Floods in Nepal, I compiled a list of descriptive identifiers of unidentified people lost in the flood, by scanning their images from the Nepal Police Website. The list included distinct tattoos, jewellery, in some cases clothing.  This list, or non graphic identification aid was created with the sole purpose and goal that family members and close friends of people who are missing, would be able to go through the list for possible identification, without having to look through the graphic and distressing images of 1300+ bodies on the website and search for missing loved ones. This is challenging to do even for volunteers like us, but for family members, the pain and suffering this would inflict while already vulnerable and hurting, would be unfathomable.  After posting this list to Facebook groups in Nepal, quite a few people reached out to me regarding family members they were looking for; family members who are STILL missing. Ellie Loveless created a group called "Rasuwa Nepal Flood and Missing Person Matching" with a few volunteers including Monika Alea Patterson who has been passionately and tirelessly working to match the unidentified bodies to people missing during the flood. She's an expert at using AI tools and technical software to enhance images, create a database, research and gather information. Sreemati Sen and Gaby van Haren big shoutouts to you both for your dedicated and compassionate efforts everyday.  A comment on a post of mine struck me, where someone asked me if I could perhaps create a graphic representation of the descriptive list I had first created. This is not forensic software, this isn't 100% accurate, but it is a graphic illustration or sketch created with AI tools, of distinct and recognizable identification such as tattoos and clear visible features of the bodies listed on the website. This took me a while to do, as I wanted each image to represent the person on the Nepal Police website as best as possible, so I took my time with each image. This was entirely done on my phone, as I don't have a laptop at the moment. It took a lot of alterations to ensure that each image was as close to the depiction of the unidentified person as possible, and as respectful as possible in order to maintain the dignity of the person and their families involved. It is still a work in progress as each day, more bodies are added to the Nepal Police database. Unfortunately, they've started blurring and pixelating the images, due to which we can see the outline of a tattoo or a comment that mentions the tattoo or jewellery under special remarks, but the image is indistinguishable. This has made our task several times harder.  It is important to note that deterioration due to being in the water for extended periods, traumatic physical injuries and bruises alter body structure, so these illustrations cannot be completely accurate. They're just illustrative depictions of what the person could have looked like. The tattoos, clothing and jewellery on the other hand, is a very close likeness as I've tailored it to look as close to the original reference as possible, including the placement on the body.  If you believe you recognise someone or a tattoo that is familiar, do reach out to me personally for the unaltered image. Share this post with everyone who is connected to the Nepal floods as we're trying to reunite people with their families.  We're volunteers, doing this without wanting anything in return except for people to share this post, this list, this group, so that family members and friends may be able to recognise and take home their loved ones, to gain closure, to grieve, to find peace.  Please share this with anyone who may need it. You never know who it may help.
